output_text:
Laravel app: INERTIA v2, FORTIFY v1, LARAVEL v12, PROMPTS v0, WAYFINDER v0, BOOST v2, MCP v0, PAIL v1, PINT v1, SAIL v1, PEST v4, PHPUNIT v12.

You MUST activate the relevant skill whenever you work in that domain—don't wait until you're stuck:
- `wayfinder-development` when referencing backend routes in frontend components, importing from `@/actions` or `@/routes`, calling Laravel routes from TypeScript, or using Wayfinder route functions.
- `pest-testing` for tests, assertions, Livewire/browser testing, debugging failures, datasets/mocking, or test-related requests.

You must follow all existing code conventions used in this application. When creating or editing a file, check sibling files for the correct structure, approach, and naming.
Use descriptive names; reuse existing components.
Do not create verification scripts or tinker when tests cover that functionality and prove they work.
Stick to existing directory structure; don't create new base folders without approval.
Do not change the application's dependencies without approval.
You must only create documentation files if explicitly requested by the user.
Be concise in your explanations.
Use Laravel Boost tools.
Use the `list-artisan-commands` tool when you need to call an Artisan command to double-check the available parameters.
Use `get-absolute-url` for project URLs.
Use `tinker` for PHP/Eloquent debugging; `database-query` for read-only database access; `database-schema` before migrations/models; `browser-logs` for recent browser logs only.
Use `search-docs` before code changes for version-specific Laravel/ecosystem documentation. Use multiple broad topic queries; do not add package names to queries.

Always use curly braces for control structures, even for single-line bodies.
Use PHP 8 constructor property promotion in `__construct()`.
Do not allow empty `__construct()` methods with zero parameters unless the constructor is private.
Always use explicit return type declarations for methods and functions.
Use appropriate PHP type hints for method parameters.
Prefer PHPDoc blocks over inline comments. Never use comments within the code itself unless the logic is exceptionally complex.
Use TitleCase Enum keys and useful array-shape PHPDocs.

The application uses Laravel Herd at `https?://[kebab-case-project-dir].test`. You must not run any commands to make the site available via HTTP(S). It is always available through Laravel Herd.

Every change must be programmatically tested. Write a new test or update an existing test, then run the affected tests to make sure they pass.
Run the minimum number of tests needed. Use `php artisan test --compact` with a specific filename or filter.

Use `Inertia::render()` and pages in `resources/js/pages`. ALWAYS use `search-docs` for Inertia documentation. Deferred props require an empty pulsing/animated skeleton.
Activate `wayfinder-development` for frontend backend routes.

Use `php artisan make:` for new files and `php artisan make:class` for generic classes. Pass `--no-interaction` to all Artisan commands and correct `--options`.
Prefer typed Eloquent relationships, models, eager loading, and `Model::query()`; avoid `DB::`.
Always create Form Request classes with rules and custom messages.
Use built-in authentication/authorization, named routes and `route()`, and queued jobs with `ShouldQueue`.
Use environment variables only in configuration files - never use the `env()` function directly outside of config files.
